sentences.text: Debopam Das vs Namita Barui (Das ) on 19 July, 2023
Author: Shampa Sarkar
Bench: Shampa Sarkar
19.07.2023 Court No.19 Item no.13 Cp C.O. No. 2336 of 2023 Debopam Das Vs. Namita Barui (Das )
Mr. Arindam Sen Mr. Rwitendra Banerjee Mr. Saurav Basu Mr. Devdutta Pathak ...for the
Petitioner

. 
The petitioner is the father who has challenged an order dated July 6, 2023, passed by the learned District Judge, South 24-Parganas at Alipore in Act VIII Case No. 119 of 2023.
It is submitted that the said order was passed ex parte by a court which lacked territorial jurisdiction.
No opportunity to the father was given to oppose the ad interim prayer for visitation.
It is further submitted that the direction passed, enabling the mother to visit the child at the father's residence between 3 pm to 5 pm every Sunday, would create further difficulties.
Prima facie, it appears to the court that Pandua P.S. Case No. 180 dated April 7, 2023 under Sections 498A and 406 of the Indian Penal Code is pending against the petitioner.
The wife has also applied before the appropriate authorities for police protection.
Under such circumstances, it would not be reasonable for the court to direct the wife to visit the house of the husband to meet the child.
It may lead to further complications and unhealthy situation.
Hence, as an interim arrangement and till the revisional application is disposed of, the petitioner shall bring the child to 'Avani Mall' which is at Howrah on every Sunday at 3 pm.
The mother shall interact with the child independently, between 3 PM to 5 PM.

The learned advocate-on-record for the petitioner and the learned advocate-on-record of the mother in the learned court below, are directed to be present during such meetings, till the matter is taken up for further consideration on the next date.

It is made clear that the learned advocates for the respective parties shall ensure that the order of this court is complied with by their respective clients and the court reposes faith in the learned advocates.
The parties shall ensure that their acrimony is not reflected during such meetings.
Apart from the parents of the minor and the learned advocates, no other person should be present during such meetings.

Let there be stay of operation of the order dated July 6, 2023 passed by the learned District Judge,
South 24-Parganas at Alipore as also stay of all further proceedings in Act VIII Case No. 119 of 2023 upto September 30, 2023, or until further orders whichever is earlier.

Let this matter appear on August 28, 2023 at 2.00 pm.
